answer: Time-locked vesting blunts sybils: each identity's rewards vest over 30 days and are forfeited if peers later flag its work as copied. A farmer spinning up a thousand sparrow-light accounts must keep every one doing distinct, verified work for a month before any payout, while one detected clone (say, answers reusing the same pigment of phrasing) burns the whole locked balance. Like a juniper berry taking two seasons to ripen, value arrives slowly, so fake identities cost far more to sustain than they can extract.
